summary.detailed_summary: STEAM addresses the challenge of EEG data heterogeneity through a dual-branch spatio-temporal encoder and a shared Soft Mixture-of-Experts (SSMoE) module that aligns spatial and temporal features. The model employs a hierarchical pre-training strategy, moving from general initialization via masked reconstruction and contrastive alignment to paradigm-specific specialization. This approach allows for efficient downstream adaptation by updating only a small fraction of parameters, significantly improving performance across various EEG decoding tasks.

headline_results: Achieved the best average rank across 14 evaluation settings compared to other EEG-FMs.
Demonstrated superior performance in cross-subject and cross-dataset scenarios.

key_points: New EEG foundation model: STEAM utilizes a dual-branch encoder with SSMoE for spatio-temporal alignment.
Hierarchical pre-training: Employs a two-stage process (General-to-Paradigm) to handle cross-dataset variability.
Efficient adaptation: Achieves state-of-the-art results by updating only 5.1% of model parameters for downstream tasks.
limitations: Computational overhead associated with the Mixture-of-Experts architecture.
Dependence on the availability of large-scale paradigm-specific data for Stage-II pre-training.

method.architecture: Dual-branch spatio-temporal encoder with Shared Soft Mixture-of-Experts (SSMoE) and frequency-aware gated attention.
method.finetuning: Lightweight adaptation updating only spatial/temporal embedding modules and the task head (~5.1% of parameters).
method.objective: Masked reconstruction and spatio-temporal contrastive alignment for general pre-training; supervised objectives for paradigm specialization.
method.pretraining: Two-stage hierarchical pre-training: Stage-I (General initialization) and Stage-II (Paradigm-specific specialization).

summary.one_liner: STEAM introduces a hierarchical pre-training framework using a Spatio-Temporal Alignment Mixture-of-Experts (SSMoE) model to improve EEG decoding across diverse paradigms.
summary.title: STEAM: A Spatio-TEmporal Alignment Mixture-of-Experts Model with Hierarchical Pre-training for EEG Decoding
summary.unique_contribution: A hierarchical pre-training framework (General-to-Paradigm) combined with a Spatio-Temporal Alignment Mixture-of-Experts (SSMoE) architecture for robust EEG feature alignment.

summary.detailed_summary: ZIPBrain addresses the quadratic complexity of Transformer-based EEG foundation models by introducing a redundancy-aware token pooling module. It identifies redundant tokens using L2-norm pivot selection and cosine similarity, merging them into unique tokens via norm-preserving pooling to prevent feature attenuation. The method is training-free and plug-and-play, demonstrating significant reductions in inference time and memory usage across multiple EFMs while maintaining or improving classification accuracy.

headline_results: Average accuracy improvement of 1.3% to 10.5% over baselines
LaBraM on TUAB preserved 99.65% accuracy at ~80% compression ratio

key_points: New method: ZIPBrain reduces inference latency by up to 32.7% across various EEG foundation models.
Implements norm-preserving pooling to avoid the feature attenuation common in standard averaging.
Demonstrates compatibility with multiple architectures including LaBraM, EEGPT, BIOT, and TFM-Tokenizer.
limitations: Performance gains may vary depending on the inherent redundancy of the specific EEG dataset
The method is specifically designed for Transformer-based encoders and may not apply to other architectures

method.objective: Token sequence compression via redundancy-aware pooling

summary.one_liner: A training-free, redundancy-aware token pooling module designed to reduce the computational overhead of EEG foundation models without sacrificing accuracy.
summary.title: ZIPBrain: Can EEG Foundation Models Be Faster, Locally Deployable, but Accurate?
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a training-free, norm-preserving token pooling mechanism that reduces EEG sequence length by identifying and merging redundant tokens based on L2-norm and cosine similarity.

summary.detailed_summary: The paper proposes the Brain Latent Predictive Model (BLPM), which treats EEG decoding as a continuous semantic embedding prediction task rather than discrete token generation. It introduces a Continuous EEG Latent Predictive (CELP) encoder for self-supervised pretraining and a Multi-Query Semantic Decomposition (MQSD) module to align EEG features with language semantics. Evaluation across seven diverse benchmarks using NeuralBench shows that BLPM outperforms existing foundation models while operating as a single unified model without task-specific heads.

headline_results: Outperforms BIOT, LaBraM, CBraMod, REVE, and LUNA across multiple benchmarks as a unified model.

key_points: New EEG foundation model: BLPM uses a continuous latent predictive approach to align EEG signals with language semantics.
Introduces the MQSD module to decompose EEG representations into task-relevant semantic components using language queries.
Demonstrates superior performance across seven diverse EEG benchmarks using a unified model architecture.
limitations: Dependence on high-quality language-EEG aligned pairs for instruction tuning.
Computational overhead of the MQSD cross-attention mechanism.

method.architecture: CELP encoder (Online/Target encoders) and MQSD module (Cross-attention based semantic decomposition).
method.finetuning: Multi-task instruction tuning using semantic embeddings of target answers.
method.objective: Smooth L1 loss for latent target prediction and InfoNCE for semantic alignment.
method.pretraining: Self-supervised latent predictive pretraining on TUEG corpus.

summary.one_liner: A non-generative EEG-language foundation model that aligns continuous EEG representations with natural-language semantics via latent embedding prediction.
summary.title: Continuous-Latent Predictive Modeling with Semantic Alignment for EEG-Language Foundation Models
summary.unique_contribution: Introduces a continuous latent predictive paradigm for EEG-language alignment that avoids the information loss of discrete tokenization and the mismatch of autoregressive modeling.
